verdict.rationale: kitty ships its own remote-control interface (`kitten @`). The docs say it can open new windows, send arbitrary text to any window and change window/tab titles. A hands-on probe confirmed a full external control loop: listing window/tab/layout state as JSON, sending text, reading output back and closing windows. Nothing in the evidence shows that every UI action (layouts, resizing, themes, fonts, all mappable actions) is reachable through this interface, so UI parity is unproven. missing for 10: documented mapping showing every UI/mappable action is exposed via remote control, evidence of parity for layout, resize, theme and font changes, independent community corroboration of API completeness.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: kitty can be controlled from scripts or the shell prompt. You can open new windows, send arbitrary text input to any window, change the title of windows and tabs, etc.

`kitten @ ls` returned full window/tab/layout state as JSON, `kitten @ send-text "echo PA_PROBE_OK"` executed in the live window, `kitten @ get-text` read the output back, `kitten @ close-window` tore it down
Control it from scripts or the shell
